Article.ArticleTitle: Macrophage-derived TGF-β1 drives portal fibrosis in murine NASH.

Abstract.AbstractText: Portal fibrosis predicts outcome in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), but the cellular source of profibrotic signals is unresolved.
We used myeloid-specific Tgfb1 knockout mice fed a choline-deficient high-fat diet (CDAHFD) for 12 weeks (n = 10 per group) and validated findings in 48 human liver biopsies.

Myeloid Tgfb1 deletion reduced Sirius red-positive area by 38% (p = 0.002) and lowered portal collagen I deposition. Human portal macrophage density correlated with fibrosis stage (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Hepatic stellate cell activation markers ACTA2 and COL1A1 fell in parallel.
Macrophage-derived TGF-beta1 is a targetable driver of portal fibrosis in NASH.

Article.ArticleTitle: Hepatic stellate cell activation proceeds independently of Kupffer cell signalling.

Abstract.AbstractText: Clodronate-mediated Kupffer cell depletion did not prevent hepatic stellate cell activation in CCl4-treated mice. Alpha-smooth muscle actin induction and collagen deposition were unchanged relative to liposome controls (n = 8 per group). These data argue against an obligate macrophage requirement for stellate cell activation, at least in toxin-driven injury.

Article.ArticleTitle: Single-cell atlas of the human NASH liver identifies a scar-associated macrophage niche.

Abstract.AbstractText: Macrophage heterogeneity in human NASH has not been resolved at single-cell level.
We profiled 78,000 CD45+ cells from 12 human NASH livers and 6 healthy controls by single-cell RNA sequencing, with spatial validation by multiplex immunofluorescence.

A TREM2+ CD9+ scar-associated macrophage population expanded 4.2-fold in fibrotic livers and localised to the fibrotic septa. This population expressed TGFB1 at higher levels than resident Kupffer cells (log2FC 1.8, adjusted p < 0.001), and its abundance tracked fibrosis stage.
Scar-associated macrophages are spatially and transcriptionally positioned to deliver profibrotic signals in human NASH.

Article.ArticleTitle: Monocyte-derived macrophages progressively replace embryonic Kupffer cells during steatohepatitis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Fate-mapping with Cx3cr1-CreER and Clec4f reporter mice showed that monocyte-derived macrophages account for 62% of the hepatic macrophage pool after 16 weeks of high-fat diet, displacing embryonically derived Kupffer cells. The recruited population retained a distinct transcriptional profile, including elevated Tgfb1 and Spp1, and did not fully adopt the resident Kupffer cell identity. Ontogeny therefore predicts function within the hepatic macrophage compartment.

Article.ArticleTitle: TREM2+ macrophages restrain rather than promote fibrogenesis in experimental steatohepatitis.

Abstract.AbstractText: TREM2+ macrophages accumulate in fibrotic liver, but whether they drive or limit fibrosis is disputed.
Trem2-/- mice and myeloid-specific Trem2 deletion were subjected to CDAHFD for 12 weeks (n = 9-12 per group).

Trem2 loss increased fibrotic area by 46% (p = 0.004) and worsened hepatocyte injury. Lipid handling by macrophages was impaired, and TGF-beta1 protein in liver lysate was unchanged between genotypes.
TREM2+ macrophages are protective in this model, cautioning against interpreting their expansion as a profibrotic signature.

Article.ArticleTitle: Smad3 phosphorylation is the rate-limiting step in stellate cell transdifferentiation.

Abstract.AbstractText: Using primary human hepatic stellate cells and a Smad3 phosphomutant knock-in mouse, we show that linker-region Smad3 phosphorylation, not receptor-Smad availability, limits transdifferentiation to myofibroblasts. Blocking the linker site abolished collagen induction downstream of TGF-beta1 without affecting Smad2 signalling. The effect was reproduced pharmacologically and genetically.

Article.ArticleTitle: Portal macrophage density predicts fibrosis progression in a prospective NAFLD cohort.

Abstract.AbstractText: Whether portal macrophage burden predicts subsequent fibrosis progression in humans is unknown.
We quantified CD68+ portal macrophages in baseline biopsies from 214 patients with paired biopsies a median of 4.1 years apart.

Baseline portal macrophage density independently predicted a one-stage fibrosis progression (adjusted OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.4-3.8, p = 0.001), after adjustment for baseline fibrosis stage, BMI and diabetes. The association was absent for lobular macrophages.
Portal, but not lobular, macrophage burden is prognostic in NAFLD.

Article.ArticleTitle: Systemic TGF-β neutralisation in advanced fibrosis: a phase 2 trial terminated for toxicity.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate a neutralising anti-TGF-beta antibody in patients with bridging fibrosis due to NASH.
Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial; 96 patients randomised before early termination.

The trial was stopped after 11 cases of cutaneous keratoacanthoma and 2 cardiac valvulopathies in the treatment arm. No significant change in fibrosis stage was observed at interim analysis (p = 0.41).
Systemic TGF-beta blockade carries unacceptable toxicity; cell-type-restricted strategies merit evaluation.
